contexts: three nursing shifts, night staffing thinner
no fixed escalation route for positive screens
reading: Screening sits between two pressures: the start of a shift, when nurses have least time, and the night, when waking a patient to screen feels wrong. The retrieved evidence places the failures at night, at weekends and in patients with dementia or sensory loss (claims c1 and c3), and shows that documentation overstates what was done (claim c2). Even a completed positive screen often waits a day for review (claim c4), which feeds the belief that screening is futile. Measuring each step, from list to screen to review, is the basis for any later change.

summary: Map traces the screening pathway from eligible patient-shift to medical review and marks where the retrieved evidence says it fails.
